books.section: Topic 6.9 Responses to Immigration in the Gilded Age

stimulus.text:
Share of all immigrants to the United States, by country of birth (percent).

| Country | 1861–1870 | 1891–1900 |
| Great Britain | 24.5 | 7.5 |
| Ireland | 18.8 | 10.0 |
| Germany | 34.0 | 14.0 |
| Austria-Hungary | 0.3 | 16.0 |
| Russia and Poland | 0.2 | 14.0 |
| Italy | 0.5 | 18.0 |
stimulus.source_note: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 11th edition (1911), article “Migration,” table of nationality of immigrants, compiled from official United States immigration figures. Public domain.

stem: According to the table, which group made up the largest share of immigrants in 1891-1900?

options.misconception: Picks a country whose share had fallen sharply by the 1890s.
Picks the largest source of the 1860s instead of the 1890s.
Picks a fast-growing group that still trails Italy.

rationales.A: Great Britain stands at 7.5 in 1891-1900, far below Italy at 18.0. Britain had faded as a source by then.
rationales.B: Germany stands at 14.0 in 1891-1900, below Italy at 18.0. Germany was the largest source thirty years earlier, not in the 1890s.
rationales.C: Russia and Poland stand at 14.0 in 1891-1900, below Italy at 18.0. They had grown fast, but not past Italy.
rationales.D: Italy stands at 18.0 in the 1891-1900 column, higher than Austria-Hungary at 16.0 and every other country in the table. No other group holds a larger share in that decade.
rationales.general:
Compare the 1891-1900 column row by row before choosing.
1. Great Britain stands at 7.5 and Ireland at 10.0.
2. Germany stands at 14.0, and Russia and Poland at 14.0.
3. Austria-Hungary stands at 16.0, and Italy at 18.0.
4. So Italy holds the largest share in 1891-1900.
Remember: on a table with two columns, read the column the question names.
